summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with recurrent abdominal pain, coffee-ground emesis, and a recent episode of syncope. Imaging and endoscopy showed no acute pathology, but findings suggested possible gastritis exacerbated by H. pylori and prednisone use. Chronic pancreatitis was also considered a contributor to her pain. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and transitioned from IV to rectal hydromorphone for pain control with good effect. H. pylori treatment was initiated, and plans were made to transition from prednisone to methotrexate for Sjogren’s management. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home tolerating oral intake with follow-up arranged. Syncope was attributed to POTS and dehydration, with no further episodes during admission.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
